name: PierceMQ
description: A distributed task queue built in Go on Redis Streams and PostgreSQL, designed for high-throughput, low-latency delivery. Built to learn distributed primitives hands-on: persistence, retries, and at-least-once semantics.

name: Contyard
description: A real-time TUI for monitoring and managing Docker containers on a local or remote host. Built to make container state readable at a glance without leaving the terminal.

name: PrepPulse
description: A terminal tool for exploring large tabular datasets, with text-based charts (histograms, scatter plots) and basic statistical summaries. Built for quick data sanity-checks without opening a notebook.

name: WCTool
description: A Go reimplementation of the classic Unix wc utility for word, line, and byte counts. A small exercise in CLI design, flags, and efficient file I/O.

name: Social-Media
description: A JavaScript full-stack social platform inspired by Facebook, from my freelance MERN period. Covers auth, posts, and feeds — the kind of CRUD and data-modeling work behind most small-business client sites.

name: PathFindingVisualization
description: A Python visualization of the A* pathfinding algorithm. Pick start and end points and watch the search expand toward the shortest path — an early algorithms-learning project.

name: SudokuSolver
description: A Sudoku solver using a backtracking algorithm with a Pygame GUI. An early project for practicing recursion and simple UI work.

name: WeatherApp
description: A small weather app built with Flask on the OpenWeather API. From the early learning period — fetching, rendering, and wiring a third-party API end to end.
